central_question: Can a cigarette-equivalent make pollution understandable without becoming medically misleading?

verified_claims.claim: Cigarette-equivalent pollution is a risk analogy built around PM2.5 exposure, not a literal statement that polluted air delivers the same chemical dose as cigarettes.
PM2.5 concentration, AQI, annual exposure and short-term spikes are different measures and must not be used interchangeably.
CO2 flight-equivalent comparisons translate emissions into familiar travel units but depend on assumptions such as distance, cabin class and non-CO2 effects.

myth_or_uncertainty_notes: Keep chapter tied to human-scale measurement, not an air-pollution guide.
visual_opportunities: [VISUAL: PM2.5 concentration to cigarette-equivalent concept graphic — with explicit analogy label]
prohibited_or_unsupported_claims: Polluted air literally equals smoking the same number of cigarettes.
A single pollution spike equals long-term exposure.
